newsitem.title: USA: CBOT August soybeans fall sharply, wheat also down.
newsitem.headline: CBOT August soybeans fall sharply, wheat also down.

text.p: CBOT August soybeans opened sharply lower in fast trade on a weekly crush figure that was below expectations and on weakness in cash basis levels, pit sources said.
Wheat futures also fell in fast trade after the U.S. Agriculture Department put U.S. winter wheat output at 1.781 billion bushels, above expectations for 1.687 billion bushels.
"It's because the crush was so bad," one CBOT trader said, referring to reasons for the sharp drop in old crop soybeans.
The National Oilseed Processors Association on Friday put weekly soybean crushings at 23 million bushels, below expectations for 23.5 to 24.5 million.
Cash sources said basis levels also slipped and U.S. Gulf CIF values were down, suggesting demand was scaling back.
At 0935 CDT, soybeans were down 14 to 4-1/4 cents per bushel with August down 10 at $7.36.
Wheat was off five to 4-1/2 cents per bushel with September down five at $3.24-1/2.
